tex_content.html:
Proposition
[$\mathrm{Ad}_g$ intertwines conjugation and the exponential map]

Source: petersen:page-0156 ↗ def:pet-ch4-adjoint-action

$\mathrm{Ad}_g(\exp (tX))=\exp (t\, \mathrm{Ad}_g(X))$ for all $g\in G$, $X\in \mathfrak g$, $t\in \mathbb {R}$.
Proof

↗ prop:pet-ch4-adjoint-exp-relation

\sketch Conjugating the one-parameter subgroup $t\mapsto \exp (tX)$ by $g$ produces a one-parameter subgroup whose derivative at the identity is $\operatorname {Ad}_gX$. Uniqueness of the integral curve in subsection 4.1 identifies it with $t\mapsto \exp (t\operatorname {Ad}_gX)$.

□
